title: Rollout Undo Path and Mini-Changelog — UX Handoff
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Design a first-class ‘undo’ flow and a compact per-rollout mini-changelog in the Redwood Console. Goal is to give operators fast, reversible control over rollout actions (start/pause/abort/variant swap) while preserving an auditable lightweight history for each rollout without forcing a full incident workflow.

Why now: Customers operating Dedicated/Private deployments requested a quicker way to recover from accidental or premature rollouts. Current Console shows rollout status but lacks immediate reversible affordances and a concise action history; this causes paging to SRE or long change windows.

Scope: Visual designs, motion specs, microcopy, keyboard accessibility, QA checklist, and redlines for dev handoff. Work covers: the Rollout Inspector panel, the condensed timeline tile in Glance mode, and the rollout list rows. Backend change-log persistence is out of scope but design assumes a simple event stream (actor, action, timestamp, reason).

Design principles and constraints: 1) Low-friction: primary undo action should be 1 click (plus confirmation for destructive ops). 2) Safe: undo is time-bound and may only revert non-idempotent state changes if backend confirms revert feasibility. 3) Visible history: mini-changelog shows last 5 actions, actor initials, short rationale. 4) Non-intrusive: undo affordance should not increase noise for normal, successful rollouts. 5) Accessible: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels, and motion reduction respected.

Core UI proposals: 1) Rollout Inspector header: add a contextual primary action dropdown with: Undo (if available), Pause, Abort, Promote. Undo is only enabled when a reversible action exists and displays a countdown badge (e.g., "Undo available — 2m:34s"). 2) Mini-changelog: condensed horizontal list under header with up to 5 items rendered as chips: [time] [actor initials] [action verb] [very short reason]. Hover expands to full sentence. Mobile/tiny widths collapse to a single summarizing chip with "+N". 3) Undo modal: single-column modal with clear state summary, reversible impacts list, confirmation checkbox ("I understand this will revert X"), and an optional free-text revert reason (for audit). 4) Snackbars: optimistic UI—show an inline transient banner on success with "Undo" button available for the remaining countdown window. 5) Motion: undo countdown uses a subtle linear progress bar (500ms update tick) and prefers reduced-motion mode when OS preference is set.

Accessibility & copy: 1) Microcopy for Undo: title "Revert recent change?"; body: "This will revert the deployment action taken by <actor> at <time>. Resources affected: <list>." CTA labels: "Revert change" (danger), "Cancel". 2) Keyboard: make Undo accessible via Enter on focused banner and Esc to dismiss modal. 3) ARIA live regions for success/failure to assistive tech.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Auto-undo vs manual: we avoid automatic rollbacks to reduce surprising behavior—users must confirm. 2) Long undo windows: keeping windows long increases chance of confusion; we recommend a configurable default (3 minutes) and allow enterprise override in Dedicated. 3) Changelog fidelity: full audit logs remain in Compliance/Audit logs; mini-changelog is intentionally lightweight for operational readability.

Handoff notes for engineering: tokens, spacing, and motion easing included. Provide Figma frame names and CSS token mapping below. See attachments for prototypes and detailed motion JSON.

Acceptance criteria (see list) must be satisfied before marking Done.
acceptance_criteria: Undo action visible in Rollout Inspector when a reversible event occurred within configured window
Undo modal copies match approved microcopy and include reversible impacts summary
Mini-changelog shows last 5 actions in correct causal order and truncates on small viewports
Snackbars appear after actions with an active Undo button and countdown matches modal state
Reduced motion respected via prefers-reduced-motion; progress bar hidden when reduced
Keyboard navigation: undo affordance reachable via Tab, Enter triggers confirm dialog, Esc closes
Design tokens and CSS variable mapping included in handoff and example component states delivered
comments: 2026-02-12 — AP: Initial mock uploaded to Figma. Left two options for Undo placement (header dropdown vs transient snackbar). Requested engineering feasibility input on optimistic rollback behavior.

2026-02-17 — HC: Reviewed with Eng lead (Miguel Santos). Backend supports lightweight revert flag but cannot guarantee atomic revert for variant-swap; added unavoidable 'revert not guaranteed' warning pattern. Action: update modal copy to reflect this.
2026-02-22 — AP: Updated microcopy after legal/security suggested audit trace capture; added optional revert reason field and guidance for enterprise audits.
2026-02-25 — Product review (Nina Park): Requested 2m default undo window be configurable per org. Marked as dependency for Dedicated rollout policies (PM-4021).

2026-03-01 — Design critique: Stakeholders preferred header placement (consistent with other primary rollout actions). Suggested stronger visual distinction for destructive revert (red outline + subtle icon).
2026-03-03 — HC: Prepared dev handoff frames and token mapping. Left follow-up tasks for QA on keyboard flows and mobile collapse behavior. See sub-issues for QA tasks.
2026-03-05 — AP: Final pass on accessible labels and reduced-motion handling. Requesting design sign-off and assignment to Eng for implementation sprint.
Open follow-ups: create e2e tests for undo window expiry, backend telemetry mapping for mini-changelog events, and update Console docs (ops playbook)
